short_description: Wheel speed sensor, steer axle left, sensor air gap too large

short_description: Exhaust gas temperature sensor (SCR inlet/outlet) circuit open

Repair open or shorted wiring, reseal the splice, clear codes and confirm the reading tracks plausibly

The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than reading the switch directly, so the fault is a link problem until the body controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the body controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

short_description: Transmission selected gear reported by the module as internally defective

short_description: Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) signal stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3651 (Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) signal) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

short_description: MSC inter-microcontroller communication fault
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 518267 (MSC inter-microcontroller communication link) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Engine ECU on an OEM-proprietary CAN channel or internal module link, rather than the main vehicle J1939 backbone -- a 'Machine' or implement CAN segment, a smart sensor's or actuator's own link to its controlling module, a tractor-trailer bridge, or a processor-to-processor link inside the ECU. Typical causes are a fault on that dedicated sub-network's wiring or connector, the linked smart device itself failing, or an internal ECU hardware fault that only a component replacement resolves.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)
fix_title: Replace the linked smart sensor, actuator or gateway/bridge module
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm via the OEM tool that the linked device itself, not just its wiring, has stopped communicating • 2. Remove and replace the smart sensor, actuator or gateway/bridge module • 3. Clear codes and confirm the link re-establishes on the next power cycle

fix_title: Verify power, ground and continuity on the proprietary link
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the linked device's power and ground pins and confirm battery voltage and a clean ground • 2. Check continuity and check for a short to power or ground on the dedicated sub-network pair • 3. Repair any wiring fault found
